text: ABOUT THE EDITOR Jennifer M.
text_raw:
ABOUT THE EDITOR
Jennifer M.

text: Bottomley, PhD2, MS, PT, has a Bachelor’s degree in PhysicalTtherapy from the University of Wisconsin, Madison and an advanced Master’s degree in Physical Therapy from the MGH Institute of Health Professionals, Boston, Mass.
text_raw:
Bottomley, PhD2, MS, PT, has a Bachelor’s degree in
PhysicalTtherapy from the University of Wisconsin, Madison and
an advanced Master’s degree in Physical Therapy from the MGH
Institute of Health Professionals, Boston, Mass.

text: She has a combined intercollegiate Doctoral degree in Gerontology and Health Science and Service Administration and a second PhD from The Union Institute in Health Science in Administration, Legislation, and Policy Management with a specialty in gerontology.
text_raw:
She has a combined
intercollegiate Doctoral degree in Gerontology and Health Science
and Service Administration and a second PhD from The Union
Institute in Health Science in Administration, Legislation, and
Policy Management with a specialty in gerontology.

text: She has prac- ticed since 1974 in acute care, home care, outpatient clinics, nursing homes, and long-term care facilities.
text_raw:
She has prac-
ticed since 1974 in acute care, home care, outpatient clinics, nursing
homes, and long-term care facilities.

text: Currently, she works as an independent consultant setting up rehabilitation services in nursing homes and outpatient, home, and community settings in the Northeast and Pacific Northwest and serves on advisory boards for the Office of the Surgeon General and the Office on Women’s Health in the Department of Health and Human Services.
text_raw:
Currently, she works as an

text: PREFACE Haven’t you always wished that all of the information you’ve learned in your physical therapy education could be easily accessed from one source?
text_raw:
PREFACE
Haven’t you always wished that all of the information you’ve
learned in your physical therapy education could be easily accessed
from one source?

text: Educating physical therapy professionals requires the acquisition of volumes of knowledge and skills in a relatively short period of time.
text_raw:
Educating physical therapy professionals requires
the acquisition of volumes of knowledge and skills in a relatively
short period of time.

text: The quantity of knowledge required for the practice of high quality physical therapy, though learned and stored, is often difficult to retrieve.
text_raw:
The quantity of knowledge required for the
practice of high quality physical therapy, though learned and
stored, is often difficult to retrieve.

text: It is with this in mind that the Quick Reference Dictionary for Physical Therapy, Second Edition has been created.
text_raw:
It is with this in mind that the
Quick Reference Dictionary for Physical Therapy, Second Edition has
been created.

text: This dictionary starts with a dictionary of commonly utilized words and their definitions.
text_raw:
This dictionary starts with a dictionary of commonly utilized
words and their definitions.

text: Though not an exhaustive list from A to Z, the intent is to provide quick reference for vocabulary that is often encountered on a day-to-day basis as a clinician and as a student.
text_raw:
Though not an exhaustive list from A to
Z, the intent is to provide quick reference for vocabulary that is often
encountered on a day-to-day basis as a clinician and as a student.

text: In the real world, many of the words we use are abbreviated.
text_raw:
In
the real world, many of the words we use are abbreviated.

text: The appendices that follow the body of the dictionary provide lists of fre- quently used and standardized acronyms and abbreviations for words (Appendix 2), medical roots from which many words are derived (Appendix 3), commonly used acronyms for evaluative tests and measures (Appendix 4), and acronyms for organizations impor- tant to the practice of physical therapy (Appendix 5).
text_raw:
The
appendices that follow the body of the dictionary provide lists of fre-
quently used and standardized acronyms and abbreviations for
words (Appendix 2), medical roots from which many words are
derived (Appendix 3), commonly used acronyms for evaluative tests
and measures (Appendix 4), and acronyms for organizations impor-
tant to the practice of physical therapy (Appendix 5).

text: It is important that we as physical therapy professionals main- tain the highest standards of practice in the most ethical and skillful manner possible and that what we do is well documented.
text_raw:
It is important that we as physical therapy professionals main-
tain the highest standards of practice in the most ethical and skillful

text: PREAMBLE This Code of Ethics of the American Physical Therapy Association sets forth principles for the ethical practice of physical therapy.
text_raw:
PREAMBLE
This Code of Ethics of the American Physical Therapy Association
sets forth principles for the ethical practice of physical therapy.

text: All physical therapists are responsible for maintaining and promoting ethical practice.
text_raw:
All
physical therapists are responsible for maintaining and promoting
ethical practice.

text: To this end, the physical therapist shall act in the best interest of the patient/client.
text_raw:
To this end, the physical therapist shall act in the
best interest of the patient/client.

text: This Code of Ethics, adopted by the American Physical Therapy Association, shall be binding on all physical therapists.
text_raw:
This Code of Ethics, adopted by the
American Physical Therapy Association, shall be binding on all
physical therapists.

text: PRINCIPLE 1 A physical therapist shall respect the rights and dignity of all individuals and shall provide comprehensive care.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 1 
A physical therapist shall respect the rights and dignity of all
individuals and shall provide comprehensive care.

text: PRINCIPLE 2 A physical therapist shall act in a trustworthy manner toward patients/clients and in all other aspects of physical therapy practice.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 2 
A physical therapist shall act in a trustworthy manner toward
patients/clients and in all other aspects of physical therapy practice.

text: PRINCIPLE 3 A physical therapist shall comply with laws and regulations governing physical therapy and shall strive to effect changes that benefit patients/clients.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 3 
A physical therapist shall comply with laws and regulations
governing physical therapy and shall strive to effect changes that
benefit patients/clients.

text: PRINCIPLE 4 A physical therapist shall exercise sound professional judgment.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 4 
A physical therapist shall exercise sound professional judgment.

text: PRINCIPLE 5 A physical therapist shall achieve and maintain professional competence.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 5 
A physical therapist shall achieve and maintain professional
competence.

text: PRINCIPLE 6 A physical therapist shall maintain and promote high standards for physical therapy practice, education, and research.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 6 
A physical therapist shall maintain and promote high standards
for physical therapy practice, education, and research.

text: PRINCIPLE 7 A physical therapist shall seek only such remuneration as is deserved and reasonable for physical therapy services.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 7 
A physical therapist shall seek only such remuneration as is
deserved and reasonable for physical therapy services.

text: PRINCIPLE 8 A physical therapist shall provide and make available accurate and relevant information to patients/clients about their care and to the public about physical therapy.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 8 
A physical therapist shall provide and make available accurate
and relevant information to patients/clients about their care and to

text: PRINCIPLE 9 A physical therapist shall protect the public and the profession from unethical, incompetent, and illegal acts.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 9
A physical therapist shall protect the public and the profession
from unethical, incompetent, and illegal acts.

text: PRINCIPLE 10 A physical therapist shall endeavor to address the health needs of society.
text_raw:

A physical therapist shall endeavor to address the health needs
of society.

text: PRINCIPLE 11 A physical therapist shall respect the rights, knowledge, and skills of colleagues and other health care professionals.

A physical therapist shall respect the rights, knowledge, and
skills of colleagues and other health care professionals.

text: The EJC also has compiled a Compendium of Interpretations and Opinions containing statements on various ethical issues.

text: These procedures are intend- ed to enable the Association to act fairly in the performance of its responsibilities as a professional organization while safeguarding the rights of the member against whom ethics charges have been made.

These procedures are intend-
ed to enable the Association to act fairly in the performance of its
responsibilities as a professional organization while safeguarding
the rights of the member against whom ethics charges have been

text: Under the Procedural Document, a Chapter Ethics Committee (CEC) has the responsibility of investigating charges referred by the Chapter President and deciding whether to dismiss the charges (subject to the EJC’s review and approval) or to recommend to the EJC that it impose one of the four forms of disciplinary action:
text_raw:
Under the Procedural Document, a Chapter Ethics Committee
(CEC) has the responsibility of investigating charges referred by the
Chapter President and deciding whether to dismiss the charges
(subject to the EJC’s review and approval) or to recommend to the
EJC that it impose one of the four forms of disciplinary action:

text: (i) reprimand, (ii) probation, (iii) suspension, or (iv) expulsion.

(i)
reprimand, (ii) probation, (iii) suspension, or (iv) expulsion.

text: When a CEC recommends a punishment, the EJC may impose the sanction recommended or impose a lesser sanction (or no sanction at all), but it may not impose a more severe punishment than that recom- mended by the CEC.
text_raw:
When
a CEC recommends a punishment, the EJC may impose the sanction
recommended or impose a lesser sanction (or no sanction at all), but
it may not impose a more severe punishment than that recom-
mended by the CEC.

text: The decision of the EJC is subject to appeal to the Board of Directors.

text: AAPPPPEENNDDIIXX 77 American Physical Therapy Association Guide for Professional Conduct PURPOSE This Guide for Professional Conduct (Guide) is intended to serve physical therapists who are members of the American Physical Therapy Association (Association) in interpreting the Code of Ethics (Code) and matters of professional conduct.
text_raw:
AAPPPPEENNDDIIXX 77
American Physical Therapy Association
Guide for Professional Conduct
PURPOSE
This Guide for Professional Conduct (Guide) is intended to serve
physical therapists who are members of the American Physical
Therapy Association (Association) in interpreting the Code of Ethics
(Code) and matters of professional conduct.

text: The Guide provides guidelines by which physical therapists may determine the propri- ety of their conduct.
text_raw:
The Guide provides
guidelines by which physical therapists may determine the propri-
ety of their conduct.

text: The Code and the Guide apply to all physical therapists who are Association members.
text_raw:
The Code and the Guide apply to all physical
therapists who are Association members.

text: These guidelines are sub- ject to changes as the dynamics of the profession change and as new patterns of health care delivery are developed and accepted by the professional community and the public.
text_raw:
These guidelines are sub-
ject to changes as the dynamics of the profession change and as new
patterns of health care delivery are developed and accepted by the
professional community and the public.

text: This Guide is subject to monitoring and timely revision by the Ethics and Judicial Committee of the Association.
text_raw:
This Guide is subject to
monitoring and timely revision by the Ethics and Judicial
Committee of the Association.

text: INTERPRETING ETHICAL PRINCIPLES The interpretations expressed in this Guide are not to be consid- ered all inclusive of situations that could evolve under a specific principle of the Code but reflect the opinions, decisions, and advice of the Judicial Committee.
text_raw:
INTERPRETING ETHICAL PRINCIPLES
The interpretations expressed in this Guide are not to be consid-
ered all inclusive of situations that could evolve under a specific
principle of the Code but reflect the opinions, decisions, and advice
of the Judicial Committee.

text: While the statements of ethical principles apply universally, specific circumstances determine their appropri- ate application.
text_raw:
While the statements of ethical principles
apply universally, specific circumstances determine their appropri-
ate application.

text: Input related to current interpretations, or situations requiring interpretation, is encouraged from Association members.
text_raw:
Input related to current interpretations, or situations
requiring interpretation, is encouraged from Association members.

text: PRINCIPLE 1 Physical therapists respect the rights and dignity of all individuals.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 1
Physical therapists respect the rights and dignity of all individuals.

text: 1.1 Attitudes of Physical Therapists A.
text_raw:
1.1 Attitudes of Physical Therapists
A.

text: Physical therapists shall recognize that each individual is different from all other individuals and shall respect and be responsive to those differences.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall recognize that each individual is
different from all other individuals and shall respect and be
responsive to those differences.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists are to be guided at all times by concern for the physical, psychological, and socioeconomic welfare of those individuals entrusted to their care.
text_raw:
Physical therapists are to be guided at all times by concern
for the physical, psychological, and socioeconomic welfare
of those individuals entrusted to their care.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapists shall not engage in conduct that consti- tutes harassment or abuse of, or discrimination against, col- leagues, associates, or others.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall not engage in conduct that consti-
tutes harassment or abuse of, or discrimination against, col-
leagues, associates, or others.

text: 1.2 Confidential Information A.
text_raw:
1.2 Confidential Information
A.

text: Information relating to the physical therapist–patient rela- tionship is confidential and may not be communicated to a third party not involved in that patient’s care without the prior written consent of the patient, subject to applicable law.
text_raw:
Information relating to the physical therapist–patient rela-
tionship is confidential and may not be communicated to a
third party not involved in that patient’s care without the
prior written consent of the patient, subject to applicable law.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Information derived from component-sponsored peer review shall be held confidential by the reviewer unless written permission to release the information is obtained from the physical therapist who was reviewed.
text_raw:
Information derived from component-sponsored peer
review shall be held confidential by the reviewer unless
written permission to release the information is obtained
from the physical therapist who was reviewed.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Information derived from the working relationships of physical therapists shall be held confidential by all parties.
text_raw:
Information derived from the working relationships of
physical therapists shall be held confidential by all parties.

text: D.
text_raw: D.

text: Information may be disclosed to appropriate authorities when it is necessary to protect the welfare of an individual or the community.
text_raw:
Information may be disclosed to appropriate authorities
when it is necessary to protect the welfare of an individual
or the community.

text: Such disclosure shall be in accordance with applicable law.
text_raw:
Such disclosure shall be in accordance
with applicable law.

text: 1.3 Patient Relations Physical therapists shall not engage in any sexual relationship or activity, whether consensual or nonconsensual, with any patient while a physical therapist/patient relationship exists.
text_raw:
1.3 Patient Relations
Physical therapists shall not engage in any sexual relationship or
activity, whether consensual or nonconsensual, with any patient
while a physical therapist/patient relationship exists.

text: 1.4 Informed Consent Physical therapists shall obtain patient informed consent before treatment, to include disclosure of:
text_raw:
1.4 Informed Consent
Physical therapists shall obtain patient informed consent before
treatment, to include disclosure of:

text: (i) the nature of the proposed inter- vention, (ii) material risks of harm or complications, (iii) reasonable alternatives to the proposed intervention, and (iv) goals of treatment.
text_raw:
(i) the nature of the proposed inter-
vention, (ii) material risks of harm or complications, (iii) reasonable
alternatives to the proposed intervention, and (iv) goals of treatment.

text: PRINCIPLE 2 Physical therapists comply with the laws and regulations gov- erning the practice of physical therapy.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 2
Physical therapists comply with the laws and regulations gov-
erning the practice of physical therapy.

text: 2.1 Professional Practice Physical therapists shall provide consultation, evaluation, treat- ment, and preventive care, in accordance with the laws and regula- tions of the jurisdiction(s) in which they practice.
text_raw:
2.1 Professional Practice
Physical therapists shall provide consultation, evaluation, treat-
ment, and preventive care, in accordance with the laws and regula-
tions of the jurisdiction(s) in which they practice.

text: PRINCIPLE 3 Physical therapists accept responsibility for the exercise of sound judgment.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 3
Physical therapists accept responsibility for the exercise of
sound judgment.

text: 3.1 Acceptance of Responsibility A.
text_raw:
3.1 Acceptance of Responsibility
A.

text: Upon accepting a patient/client for provision of physical therapy services, physical therapists shall assume the responsibility for examining, evaluating, and diagnosing that individual; prognosis and intervention; reexamination and modification of the plan of care; and maintaining ade- quate records of the case including progress reports.
text_raw:
Upon accepting a patient/client for provision of physical
therapy services, physical therapists shall assume the
responsibility for examining, evaluating, and diagnosing
that individual; prognosis and intervention; reexamination
and modification of the plan of care; and maintaining ade-
quate records of the case including progress reports.

text: Physical therapists establish the plan of care and provide and/or supervise the appropriate intervention.
text_raw:
Physical therapists establish the plan of care and provide
and/or supervise the appropriate intervention.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: If the diagnostic process reveals findings that are outside the scope of the physical therapist’s knowledge, experience, or expertise, the physical therapist shall so inform the patient/client and refer to an appropriate practitioner.
text_raw:
If the diagnostic process reveals findings that are outside the
scope of the physical therapist’s knowledge, experience, or
expertise, the physical therapist shall so inform the
patient/client and refer to an appropriate practitioner.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Regardless of practice setting, physical therapists shall maintain the ability to make independent judgments.
text_raw:
Regardless of practice setting, physical therapists shall
maintain the ability to make independent judgments.

text: D.
text_raw: D.

text: The physical therapist shall not provide physical therapy services to a patient while under the influence of a substance that impairs his or her ability to do so safely.
text_raw:
The physical therapist shall not provide physical therapy
services to a patient while under the influence of a substance
that impairs his or her ability to do so safely.

text: E.
text_raw: E.

text: When the patient is referred from another practitioner, the physical therapist shall communicate the findings of the examination, the diagnosis, the proposed intervention, and reexamination findings (as indicated) to the referring practi- tioner and any other appropriate individuals involved in the patient’s care, while maintaining standards of confidentiality.
text_raw:
When the patient is referred from another practitioner, the
physical therapist shall communicate the findings of the
examination, the diagnosis, the proposed intervention, and
reexamination findings (as indicated) to the referring practi-
tioner and any other appropriate individuals involved in the
patient’s care, while maintaining standards of confidentiality.

text: 3.2 Delegation of Responsibility A.
text_raw:
3.2 Delegation of Responsibility
A.

text: Physical therapists shall not delegate to a less qualified per- son any activity which requires the unique skill, knowledge, and judgment of the physical therapist.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall not delegate to a less qualified per-
son any activity which requires the unique skill, knowledge,
and judgment of the physical therapist.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: The primary responsibility for physical therapy care ren- dered by supportive personnel rests with the supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
The primary responsibility for physical therapy care ren-
dered by supportive personnel rests with the supervising
physical therapist.

text: Adequate supervision requires, at a min- imum, that a supervising physical therapist perform the fol- lowing activities:
text_raw:
Adequate supervision requires, at a min-
imum, that a supervising physical therapist perform the fol-
lowing activities:

text: Designate or establish channels of written and oral communication.
text_raw:
Designate or establish channels of written and oral 
communication.

text: APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 263
text_raw: APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 263

text: Interpret available information concerning the indi- vidual under care.
text_raw:
Interpret available information concerning the indi-
vidual under care.

text: Examine, evaluate, and determine a diagnosis.
text_raw: Examine, evaluate, and determine a diagnosis.

text: Develop plan of care, including short- and long-term goals.
text_raw:
Develop plan of care, including short- and long-term
goals.

text: Select and delegate appropriate tasks of plan of care.
text_raw: Select and delegate appropriate tasks of plan of care.

text: Assess competence of supportive personnel to per- form assigned tasks.
text_raw:
Assess competence of supportive personnel to per-
form assigned tasks.

text: Direct and supervise supportive personnel in delegat- ed tasks.
text_raw:
Direct and supervise supportive personnel in delegat-
ed tasks.

text: Identify and document precautions, special problems, contraindications, goals, anticipated progress, and plans for reevaluation.
text_raw:
Identify and document precautions, special problems,
contraindications, goals, anticipated progress, and
plans for reevaluation.

text: Reevaluate, adjust plan of care when necessary, per- form final evaluation, and establish follow-up plan.
text_raw:
Reevaluate, adjust plan of care when necessary, per-
form final evaluation, and establish follow-up plan.

text: 3.3 Provision of Services A.
text_raw:
3.3 Provision of Services
A.

text: Physical therapists shall recognize the individual’s freedom of choice in selection of physical therapy services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall recognize the individual’s freedom
of choice in selection of physical therapy services.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists’ professional practices and their adher- ence to ethical principles of the Association shall take pref- erence over business practices.
text_raw:
Physical therapists’ professional practices and their adher-
ence to ethical principles of the Association shall take pref-
erence over business practices.

text: Provisions of services for personal financial gain rather than for the need of the indi- vidual receiving the services are unethical.
text_raw:
Provisions of services for
personal financial gain rather than for the need of the indi-
vidual receiving the services are unethical.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: When physical therapists judge that an individual will no longer benefit from their services, they shall so inform the individual receiving the services.
text_raw:
When physical therapists judge that an individual will no
longer benefit from their services, they shall so inform the
individual receiving the services.

text: Physical therapists shall avoid overutilization of their services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall
avoid overutilization of their services.

text: D.
text_raw: D.

text: In the event of elective termination of a physical thera- pist/patient relationship by the physical therapist, the ther- apist should take steps to transfer the care of the patient, as appropriate, to another provider.
text_raw:
In the event of elective termination of a physical thera-
pist/patient relationship by the physical therapist, the ther-
apist should take steps to transfer the care of the patient, as
appropriate, to another provider.

text: E.
text_raw: E.

text: Physical therapists shall recognize that third-party payer contracts may limit, in one form or another, provision of physical therapy services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall recognize that third-party payer
contracts may limit, in one form or another, provision of
physical therapy services.

text: Physical therapists shall inform patients of any known limitations.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall inform
patients of any known limitations.

text: Third-party limitations do not absolve the physical therapist from adherence to eth- ical principles.
text_raw:
Third-party limitations
do not absolve the physical therapist from adherence to eth-
ical principles.

text: Physical therapists shall avoid underutiliza- tion of their services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall avoid underutiliza-
tion of their services.

text: 3.4 Practice Arrangements A.
text_raw:
3.4 Practice Arrangements
A.

text: Participation in a business, partnership, corporation, or other entity does not exempt the physical therapist, whether employer, partner, or stockholder, either individually or col- lectively, from the obligation of promoting and maintaining the ethical principles of the Association.
text_raw:
Participation in a business, partnership, corporation, or
other entity does not exempt the physical therapist, whether
employer, partner, or stockholder, either individually or col-
lectively, from the obligation of promoting and maintaining
the ethical principles of the Association.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists shall advise their employer(s) of any employer practice which causes a physical therapist to be in conflict with the ethical principles of the Association.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall advise their employer(s) of any
employer practice which causes a physical therapist to be in
conflict with the ethical principles of the Association.

text: Physical therapist employees shall attempt to rectify aspects of their employment which are in conflict with the ethical principles of the Association.
text_raw:
Physical therapist employees shall attempt to rectify aspects
of their employment which are in conflict with the ethical
principles of the Association.

text: PRINCIPLE 4 Physical therapists maintain and promote high standards for physical therapy practice, education, and research.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 4
Physical therapists maintain and promote high standards for
physical therapy practice, education, and research.

text: 4.1 Continued Education A.
text_raw:
4.1 Continued Education
A.

text: Physical therapists shall participate in educational activities which enhance their basic knowledge and provide new knowledge.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall participate in educational activities
which enhance their basic knowledge and provide new
knowledge.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Whenever physical therapists provide continuing educa- tion, they shall ensure that course content, objectives, and responsibilities of the instructional faculty are accurately reflected in the promotion of the course.
text_raw:
Whenever physical therapists provide continuing educa-
tion, they shall ensure that course content, objectives, and
responsibilities of the instructional faculty are accurately
reflected in the promotion of the course.

text: 4.2 Review and Self-Assessment A.
text_raw:
4.2 Review and Self-Assessment
A.

text: Physical therapists shall provide for utilization review of their services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall provide for utilization review of
their services.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists shall demonstrate their commitment to quality assurance by peer review and self-assessment.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall demonstrate their commitment to
quality assurance by peer review and self-assessment.

text: 4.3 Research A.
text_raw:
4.3 Research
A.

text: Physical therapists shall support research activities that con- tribute knowledge for improved patient care.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall support research activities that con-
tribute knowledge for improved patient care.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists engaged in research shall ensure:
text_raw: Physical therapists engaged in research shall ensure:

text: 1. the consent of subjects;
text_raw: 1. the consent of subjects;

text: 2. confidentiality of the data on individual subjects and the personal identities of the subjects;
text_raw:
2. confidentiality of the data on individual subjects and the
personal identities of the subjects;

text: APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 265
text_raw: APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 265

text: 3. well-being of all subjects in compliance with facility reg- ulations and laws of the jurisdiction in which the research is conducted;
4. the absence of fraud and plagiarism;
text_raw: 4. the absence of fraud and plagiarism;

text: 5. full disclosure of support received;
text_raw: 5. full disclosure of support received;

text: 6. appropriate acknowledgment of individuals making a contribution to the research; and 7. that animal subjects used in research are treated humane- ly and in compliance with facility regulations and laws of the jurisdiction in which the research experimentation is conducted.
text_raw:
6. appropriate acknowledgment of individuals making a 
contribution to the research; and
7. that animal subjects used in research are treated humane-
ly and in compliance with facility regulations and laws of
the jurisdiction in which the research experimentation is 
conducted.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapists shall report to appropriate authorities any acts in the conduct or presentation of research that appear unethical or illegal.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall report to appropriate authorities
any acts in the conduct or presentation of research that
appear unethical or illegal.

text: 4.4 Education A.
text_raw:
4.4 Education
A.

text: Physical therapists shall support quality education in aca- demic and clinical settings.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall support quality education in aca-
demic and clinical settings.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists functioning in the educational role are responsible to the students, the academic institutions, and the clinical settings for promoting ethical conduct in educational activities.
text_raw:
Physical therapists functioning in the educational role are
responsible to the students, the academic institutions, and the
clinical settings for promoting ethical conduct in educational
activities.

text: Whenever possible, the educator shall ensure:
text_raw: Whenever possible, the educator shall ensure:

text: 1. the rights of students in the academic and clinical setting;
text_raw: 1. the rights of students in the academic and clinical setting;

text: 2. appropriate confidentiality of personal information;
text_raw: 2. appropriate confidentiality of personal information;

text: 3. professional conduct towards the student during the aca- demic and clinical education processes; and 4. assignment to clinical settings prepared to give the stu- dent a learning experience.
text_raw:
3. professional conduct towards the student during the aca-
demic and clinical education processes; and
4. assignment to clinical settings prepared to give the stu-
dent a learning experience.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Clinical educators are responsible for reporting to the aca- demic program student conduct which appears to be uneth- ical or illegal.
text_raw:
Clinical educators are responsible for reporting to the aca-
demic program student conduct which appears to be uneth-
ical or illegal.

text: PRINCIPLE 5 Physical therapists seek remuneration for their services that is deserved and reasonable.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 5
Physical therapists seek remuneration for their services that is
deserved and reasonable.

text: 5.1 Fiscally Sound Remuneration A.
text_raw:
5.1 Fiscally Sound Remuneration
A.

text: Physical therapists shall never place their own financial interest above the welfare of individuals under their care.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall never place their own financial
interest above the welfare of individuals under their care.

text: 266 Appendix 7
text_raw: 266 Appendix 7

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Fees for physical therapy services should be reasonable for the service performed, considering the setting in which it is provided, practice costs in the geographic area, judgment of other organizations, and other relevant factors.
text_raw:
Fees for physical therapy services should be reasonable for
the service performed, considering the setting in which it is
provided, practice costs in the geographic area, judgment of
other organizations, and other relevant factors.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapists should attempt to ensure that providers, agencies, or other employers adopt physical therapy fee schedules that are reasonable and that encourage access to necessary services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists should attempt to ensure that providers,
agencies, or other employers adopt physical therapy fee
schedules that are reasonable and that encourage access to
necessary services.

text: 5.2 Business Practices/Fee Arrangements A.
text_raw:
5.2 Business Practices/Fee Arrangements
A.

text: Physical therapists shall not:
text_raw: Physical therapists shall not:

text: 1. directly or indirectly request, receive, or participate in the dividing, transferring, assigning, or rebating of an un- earned fee, and 2. profit by means of a credit or other valuable considera- tion, such as an unearned commission, discount, or gra- tuity in connection with furnishing of physical therapy services.
text_raw:
1. directly or indirectly request, receive, or participate in the
dividing, transferring, assigning, or rebating of an un-
earned fee, and
2. profit by means of a credit or other valuable considera-
tion, such as an unearned commission, discount, or gra-
tuity in connection with furnishing of physical therapy
services.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Unless laws impose restrictions to the contrary, physical therapists who provide physical therapy services in a busi- ness entity may pool fees and moneys received.
text_raw:
Unless laws impose restrictions to the contrary, physical
therapists who provide physical therapy services in a busi-
ness entity may pool fees and moneys received.

text: Physical therapists may divide or apportion these fees and moneys in accordance with the business agreement.
text_raw:
Physical
therapists may divide or apportion these fees and moneys in
accordance with the business agreement.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapists may enter into agreements with organi- zations to provide physical therapy services if such agree- ments do not violate the ethical principles of the Association.
text_raw:
Physical therapists may enter into agreements with organi-
zations to provide physical therapy services if such agree-
ments do not violate the ethical principles of the
Association.

text: 5.3 Endorsement of Equipment or Services A.
text_raw:
5.3 Endorsement of Equipment or Services
A.

text: Physical therapists shall not use influence upon individuals under their care or their families for utilization of equipment or services based upon the direct or indirect financial interest of the physical therapist in such equipment or services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall not use influence upon individuals
under their care or their families for utilization of equipment
or services based upon the direct or indirect financial interest
of the physical therapist in such equipment or services.

text: Realizing that these individuals will normally rely on the physical therapists’ advice, their best interest must always be maintained as well as their right of free choice relating to the use of any equipment or service.
text_raw:
Realizing that these individuals will normally rely on the
physical therapists’ advice, their best interest must always be
maintained as well as their right of free choice relating to the
use of any equipment or service.

text: While it cannot be considered unethical for physical therapists to own or have a financial interest in equipment companies or services, they must act in accordance with law and make full disclosure of their interest whenever such companies or services become the source of equipment or services for individuals under their care.
text_raw:
While it cannot be considered
unethical for physical therapists to own or have a financial
interest in equipment companies or services, they must act in
accordance with law and make full disclosure of their interest
whenever such companies or services become the source of
equipment or services for individuals under their care.

text: APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 267
text_raw: APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 267

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists may be remunerated for endorsement or advertisement of equipment or services to the lay public, physical therapists, or other health professionals provided they disclose any financial interest in the production, sale, or distribution of said equipment or services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists may be remunerated for endorsement or
advertisement of equipment or services to the lay public,
physical therapists, or other health professionals provided
they disclose any financial interest in the production, sale, or
distribution of said equipment or services.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: In endorsing or advertising equipment or services, physical therapists shall use sound professional judgment and shall not give the appearance of Association endorsement.
text_raw:
In endorsing or advertising equipment or services, physical
therapists shall use sound professional judgment and shall
not give the appearance of Association endorsement.

text: 5.4 Gifts and Other Considerations A.
text_raw:
5.4 Gifts and Other Considerations
A.

text: Physical therapists shall not accept nor offer gifts or other considerations with obligatory conditions attached.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall not accept nor offer gifts or other
considerations with obligatory conditions attached.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists shall not accept nor offer gifts or other considerations that affect or give an objective appearance of affecting their professional judgment.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall not accept nor offer gifts or other
considerations that affect or give an objective appearance of
affecting their professional judgment.

text: PRINCIPLE 6 Physical therapists provide accurate information to the con- sumer about the profession and about those services they provide.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 6
Physical therapists provide accurate information to the con-
sumer about the profession and about those services they provide.

text: 6.1 Information about the Profession Physical therapists shall endeavor to educate the public to an awareness of the physical therapy profession through such means as publication of articles and participation in seminars, lectures, and civic programs.
text_raw:
6.1 Information about the Profession
Physical therapists shall endeavor to educate the public to an
awareness of the physical therapy profession through such means
as publication of articles and participation in seminars, lectures, and
civic programs.

text: 6.2 Information about Services A.
text_raw:
6.2 Information about Services
A.

text: Information given to the public shall emphasize that indi- vidual problems cannot be treated without individualized evaluation and plans/programs of care.
text_raw:
Information given to the public shall emphasize that indi-
vidual problems cannot be treated without individualized
evaluation and plans/programs of care.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists may advertise their services to the public.
text_raw: Physical therapists may advertise their services to the public.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapists shall not use, or participate in the use of, any form of communication containing a false, plagiarized, fraudulent, misleading, deceptive, unfair, or sensational statement or claim.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall not use, or participate in the use of,
any form of communication containing a false, plagiarized,
fraudulent, misleading, deceptive, unfair, or sensational
statement or claim.

text: D.
text_raw: D.

text: A paid advertisement shall be identified as such unless it is apparent from the context that it is a paid advertisement.
text_raw:
A paid advertisement shall be identified as such unless it is
apparent from the context that it is a paid advertisement.

text: PRINCIPLE 7 Physical therapists accept the responsibility to protect the public and the profession from unethical, incompetent, or illegal acts.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 7
Physical therapists accept the responsibility to protect the public
and the profession from unethical, incompetent, or illegal acts.

text: 268 Appendix 7
text_raw: 268 Appendix 7

text: 7.1 Consumer Protection A.
text_raw:
7.1 Consumer Protection
A.

text: Physical therapists shall report any conduct which appears to be unethical, incompetent, or illegal.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall report any conduct which appears
to be unethical, incompetent, or illegal.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapists may not participate in any arrangements in which patients are exploited due to the referring sources enhancing their personal incomes as a result of referring for, prescribing, or recommending physical therapy.
text_raw:
Physical therapists may not participate in any arrangements
in which patients are exploited due to the referring sources
enhancing their personal incomes as a result of referring for,
prescribing, or recommending physical therapy.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapists shall be obligated to safeguard the pub- lic from underutilization or overutilization of physical ther- apy services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall be obligated to safeguard the pub-
lic from underutilization or overutilization of physical ther-
apy services.

text: 7.2 Disclosure The physical therapist shall disclose to the patient if the refer- ring practitioner derives compensation from the provision of phys- ical therapy.
text_raw:
7.2 Disclosure
The physical therapist shall disclose to the patient if the refer-
ring practitioner derives compensation from the provision of phys-
ical therapy.

text: The physical therapist shall ensure that the individual has freedom of choice in selecting a provider of physical therapy.
text_raw:
The physical therapist shall ensure that the individual
has freedom of choice in selecting a provider of physical therapy.

text: PRINCIPLE 8 Physical therapists participate in efforts to address the health needs of the public.
text_raw:
PRINCIPLE 8
Physical therapists participate in efforts to address the health
needs of the public.

text: 8.1 Pro Bono Service Physical therapists should render pro bono publico (reduced or no fee) services to patients lacking the ability to pay for services, as each physical therapist’s practice permits.
text_raw:
8.1 Pro Bono Service
Physical therapists should render pro bono publico (reduced or no
fee) services to patients lacking the ability to pay for services, as
each physical therapist’s practice permits.

text: JANUARY 1999 AMENDMENTS TO GUIDE FOR PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT The APTA’s Ethics and Judicial Committee (EJC) made a num- ber of amendments to the Guide for Professional Conduct at its January 1999 meeting.
text_raw:
JANUARY 1999 AMENDMENTS TO
GUIDE FOR PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT
The APTA’s Ethics and Judicial Committee (EJC) made a num-
ber of amendments to the Guide for Professional Conduct at its
January 1999 meeting.

text: The amendments address three areas as to which the House of Delegates (in the Support Statement for RC 18- 98) indicated that the document needed revision:
text_raw:
The amendments address three areas as to
which the House of Delegates (in the Support Statement for RC 18-
98) indicated that the document needed revision:

text: (i) diagnosis by APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 269
text_raw:
(i) diagnosis by
APTA Guide for Professional Conduct 269

text: physical therapists;
text_raw: physical therapists;

text: (ii) referral relationships, and the inappropri- ateness of using the term “prescribes” to characterize the role of a referring practitioner; and (iii) underutilization attributable to third-party limitations on the provision of physical therapy servic- es (not including limitations that give the practitioner a financial incentive to limit or curtail services).
text_raw:
(ii) referral relationships, and the inappropri-
ateness of using the term “prescribes” to characterize the role of a
referring practitioner; and (iii) underutilization attributable to
third-party limitations on the provision of physical therapy servic-
es (not including limitations that give the practitioner a financial
incentive to limit or curtail services).

text: The EJC voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by amending Section 3.1(A) to read as follows:
text_raw:
The EJC voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by
amending Section 3.1(A) to read as follows:

text: A.
text_raw: A.

text: Upon accepting a patient/client for provision of physical therapy services, physical therapists shall assume the responsibility for examining, evaluating, and diagnosing that individual; prognosis and intervention; reexamination and modification of the plan of care; and maintaining ade- quate records of the case including progress reports.
text_raw:
Upon accepting a patient/client for provision of physical
therapy services, physical therapists shall assume the
responsibility for examining, evaluating, and diagnosing
that individual; prognosis and intervention; reexamination
and modification of the plan of care; and maintaining ade-
quate records of the case including progress reports.

text: Physical therapists establish the plan of care and provide and/or supervise the appropriate intervention.
text_raw:
Physical therapists establish the plan of care and provide
and/or supervise the appropriate intervention.

text: This change makes explicit that physical therapists are responsi- ble for making diagnoses, consistent with Diagnosis by Physical Therapists (HOD 06-97-06-19).
text_raw:
This change makes explicit that physical therapists are responsi-
ble for making diagnoses, consistent with Diagnosis by Physical
Therapists (HOD 06-97-06-19).

text: The change makes the Guide for Professional Conduct more consistent with the terminology of the APTA’s Guide to Physical Therapist Practice.
text_raw:
The change makes the Guide for
Professional Conduct more consistent with the terminology of the
APTA’s Guide to Physical Therapist Practice.

text: The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by deleting Section 3.1(B) and replacing it with the following lan- guage:
text_raw:
The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct
by deleting Section 3.1(B) and replacing it with the following lan-
guage:

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: If the diagnostic process reveals findings that are outside the scope of the physical therapist’s knowledge, experience, or expertise, the physical therapist shall so inform the patient/client and refer him or her to an appropriate practi- tioner.
text_raw:
If the diagnostic process reveals findings that are outside the
scope of the physical therapist’s knowledge, experience, or
expertise, the physical therapist shall so inform the
patient/client and refer him or her to an appropriate practi-
tioner.

text: This change makes explicit that physical therapists are responsi- ble for making diagnoses, consistent with Diagnosis by Physical Therapists (HOD 06-97-06-19).
text_raw:
This change makes explicit that physical therapists are responsi-
ble for making diagnoses, consistent with Diagnosis by Physical
Therapists (HOD 06-97-06-19).

text: The replacement language derives largely from the Guide to Physical Therapist Practice (page 1 to 7, under the heading “Diagnosis”).
text_raw:
The replacement language derives
largely from the Guide to Physical Therapist Practice (page 1 to 7,
under the heading “Diagnosis”).

text: The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by adding the following new Section 3.1(E):
text_raw:
The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct
by adding the following new Section 3.1(E):

text: E.
text_raw: E.

text: When the patient is referred from another practitioner, the physical therapist shall communicate the findings of the examination, the diagnosis, the proposed intervention, and reexamination findings (as indicated) to the referring practi- tioner and any other appropriate individuals involved in the patient’s care, while maintaining standards of confidentiality.
text_raw:
When the patient is referred from another practitioner, the
physical therapist shall communicate the findings of the
examination, the diagnosis, the proposed intervention, and
reexamination findings (as indicated) to the referring practi-
tioner and any other appropriate individuals involved in the
patient’s care, while maintaining standards of confidentiality.

text: 270 Appendix 7
text_raw: 270 Appendix 7

text: This addition requires the physical therapist to engage in some communication with referring practitioners (and others, as appro- priate).
text_raw:
This addition requires the physical therapist to engage in some
communication with referring practitioners (and others, as appro-
priate).

text: Communicating reexamination findings to the referring practitioner is required only where that practitioner has so indicat- ed.
text_raw:
Communicating reexamination findings to the referring
practitioner is required only where that practitioner has so indicat-
ed.

text: This change should be understood in conjunction with the Committee’s deletion of former Section 3.4 (Referral Relationships), a Section which infelicitously used the term “prescribes” to charac- terize the role of the referring practitioner.
text_raw:
This change should be understood in conjunction with the
Committee’s deletion of former Section 3.4 (Referral Relationships),
a Section which infelicitously used the term “prescribes” to charac-
terize the role of the referring practitioner.

text: See Position on Term “Prescription” (BOD 03-93-22-59).

See Position on Term
“Prescription” (BOD 03-93-22-59).

text: The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by deleting clause 3 in Section 3.2(B) and replacing it with the fol- lowing language:

The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct
by deleting clause 3 in Section 3.2(B) and replacing it with the fol-
lowing language:

text: Examine, evaluate, and determine a diagnosis.
text_raw: Examine, evaluate, and determine a diagnosis.

text: This change makes explicit that physical therapists are responsi- ble for making diagnoses, consistent with Diagnosis by Physical Therapists (HOD 06-97-06-19).
text_raw:
This change makes explicit that physical therapists are responsi-
ble for making diagnoses, consistent with Diagnosis by Physical
Therapists (HOD 06-97-06-19).

text: The change makes the Guide for Professional Conduct more consistent with the terminology of the Guide to Physical Therapist Practice.
text_raw:
The change makes the Guide for
Professional Conduct more consistent with the terminology of the
Guide to Physical Therapist Practice.

text: The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by adding a new Section 3.3(E) to read as follows:
text_raw:
The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct
by adding a new Section 3.3(E) to read as follows:

text: E.
text_raw: E.

text: Physical therapists shall recognize that third-party payer contracts may limit, in one form or another, provision of physical therapy services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall recognize that third-party payer
contracts may limit, in one form or another, provision of
physical therapy services.

text: Physical therapists shall inform patients of any known limitations.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall inform
patients of any known limitations.

text: Third-party limitations do not absolve the physical therapist from adherence to eth- ical principles.
text_raw:
Third-party limitations
do not absolve the physical therapist from adherence to eth-
ical principles.

text: Physical therapists shall avoid underutiliza- tion of their services.
text_raw:
Physical therapists shall avoid underutiliza-
tion of their services.

text: This new Section 3.3(E) begins to address the ethical implica- tions of limitations by payers on the provision of physical therapy services.
text_raw:
This new Section 3.3(E) begins to address the ethical implica-
tions of limitations by payers on the provision of physical therapy
services.

text: In the Committee’s view, the new language extends to lim- itations on the number of visits or length of treatment for which the third party will pay, but it does not extend to situations in which a limitation takes the form of the physical therapist’s having a finan- cial incentive to limit or curtail services.
text_raw:
In the Committee’s view, the new language extends to lim-
itations on the number of visits or length of treatment for which the
third party will pay, but it does not extend to situations in which a
limitation takes the form of the physical therapist’s having a finan-
cial incentive to limit or curtail services.

text: Therefore, the new lan- guage does not require a physical therapist to inform the patient of a limitation attributable to a capitation or other arrangement that gives the physical therapy service a financial incentive to limit or curtail therapy.
text_raw:
Therefore, the new lan-
guage does not require a physical therapist to inform the patient of
a limitation attributable to a capitation or other arrangement that
gives the physical therapy service a financial incentive to limit or
curtail therapy.

text: The Committee voted to amend the Guide for Professional Conduct by deleting Section 3.4 (Referral Relationships) in its entirety, and by renumbering current Section 3.5 (Practice Arrangements) as Section 3.4.

by deleting Section 3.4 (Referral Relationships) in its entirety, and
by renumbering current Section 3.5 (Practice Arrangements) as
Section 3.4.

text: AAPPPPEENNDDIIXX 99 American Physical Therapy Association Guide for Conduct of the Affiliate Member PURPOSE This Guide is intended to serve physical therapist assistants who are affiliate members of the American Physical Therapy Association in the interpretation of the Standards of Ethical Conduct for the Physical Therapist Assistant , providing guidelines by which they may determine the propriety of their conduct.
text_raw:
AAPPPPEENNDDIIXX 99
American Physical Therapy Association
Guide for Conduct of the Affiliate Member
PURPOSE
This Guide is intended to serve physical therapist assistants who
are affiliate members of the American Physical Therapy Association
in the interpretation of the Standards of Ethical Conduct for the
Physical Therapist Assistant , providing guidelines by which they
may determine the propriety of their conduct.

text: These guidelines are subject to change as new patterns of health care delivery are devel- oped and accepted by the professional community and the public.
text_raw:
These guidelines are
subject to change as new patterns of health care delivery are devel-
oped and accepted by the professional community and the public.

text: INTERPRETING STANDARDS The interpretations expressed in this Guide are not to be consid- ered all inclusive of situations that could evolve under a specific standard of the Standards of Ethical Conduct for the Physical Therapist Assistant but reflect the opinions, decisions, and advice of the Judicial Committee.
text_raw:
INTERPRETING STANDARDS
The interpretations expressed in this Guide are not to be consid-
ered all inclusive of situations that could evolve under a specific
standard of the Standards of Ethical Conduct for the Physical Therapist
Assistant but reflect the opinions, decisions, and advice of the
Judicial Committee.

text: While the statements of ethical standards apply universally, specific circumstances determine their appropriate application.
text_raw:
While the statements of ethical standards apply
universally, specific circumstances determine their appropriate
application.

text: Input related to current interpretations, or situations requiring interpretation, is encouraged from APTA members.
text_raw:
Input related to current interpretations, or situations
requiring interpretation, is encouraged from APTA members.

text: STANDARD 1 Physical therapist assistants provide services under the supervi- sion of a physical therapist.
text_raw:
STANDARD 1
Physical therapist assistants provide services under the supervi-
sion of a physical therapist.

text: 1.1 Supervisory Relationships Physical therapist assistants shall work under the supervision and direction of a physical therapist who is properly credentialed in the jurisdiction in which the physical therapist assistant practices.
text_raw:
1.1 Supervisory Relationships
Physical therapist assistants shall work under the supervision
and direction of a physical therapist who is properly credentialed in
the jurisdiction in which the physical therapist assistant practices.

text: 1.2 Performance of Service A.
text_raw:
1.2 Performance of Service
A.

text: Physical therapist assistants may not initiate or alter a treat- ment program without prior evaluation by and approval of the supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may not initiate or alter a treat-
ment program without prior evaluation by and approval of
the supervising physical therapist.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapist assistants may modify a specific treat- ment procedure in accordance with changes in patient sta- tus.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may modify a specific treat-
ment procedure in accordance with changes in patient sta-
tus.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapist assistants may not interpret data beyond the scope of their physical therapist assistant education.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may not interpret data beyond
the scope of their physical therapist assistant education.

text: D.
text_raw: D.

text: Physical therapist assistants may respond to inquiries regarding patient status to appropriate parties within the protocol established by a supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may respond to inquiries
regarding patient status to appropriate parties within the
protocol established by a supervising physical therapist.

text: E.
text_raw: E.

text: Physical therapist assistants shall refer inquiries regarding patient prognosis to a supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants shall refer inquiries regarding
patient prognosis to a supervising physical therapist.

text: STANDARD 2 Physical therapist assistants respect the rights and dignity of all individuals.
text_raw:
STANDARD 2
Physical therapist assistants respect the rights and dignity of all
individuals.

text: 2.1 Attitudes of Physical Therapist Assistants A.
text_raw:
2.1 Attitudes of Physical Therapist Assistants
A.

text: Physical therapist assistants shall recognize that each indi- vidual is different from all other individuals and respect and be responsive to those differences.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants shall recognize that each indi-
vidual is different from all other individuals and respect and
be responsive to those differences.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapist assistants shall be guided at all times by concern for the dignity and welfare of those patients entrust- ed to their care.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants shall be guided at all times by
concern for the dignity and welfare of those patients entrust-
ed to their care.

text: C.
text_raw: C.

text: Physical therapist assistants shall not engage in conduct that constitutes harassment or abuse of, or discrimination against, colleagues, associates, or others.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants shall not engage in conduct that
constitutes harassment or abuse of, or discrimination
against, colleagues, associates, or others.

text: 2.2 Request for Release of Information Physical therapist assistants shall refer all requests for release of confidential information to the supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
2.2 Request for Release of Information
Physical therapist assistants shall refer all requests for release of
confidential information to the supervising physical therapist.

text: 2.3 Protection of Privacy Physical therapist assistants must treat as confidential all infor- mation relating to the personal conditions and affairs of the persons whom they serve.
text_raw:
2.3 Protection of Privacy
Physical therapist assistants must treat as confidential all infor-
mation relating to the personal conditions and affairs of the persons
whom they serve.

text: 2.4 Patient Relations Physical therapist assistants shall not engage in any sexual rela- tionship or activity, whether consensual or nonconsensual, with any patient while a physical therapist assistant/patient relationship exists.
text_raw:
2.4 Patient Relations
Physical therapist assistants shall not engage in any sexual rela-
tionship or activity, whether consensual or nonconsensual, with any
patient while a physical therapist assistant/patient relationship exists.

text_raw: 276 Appendix 9

text: STANDARD 3 Physical therapist assistants maintain and promote high stan- dards in the provision of services, giving the welfare of patients their highest regard.
text_raw:
STANDARD 3
Physical therapist assistants maintain and promote high stan-
dards in the provision of services, giving the welfare of patients
their highest regard.

text: 3.1 Information about Services A.
text_raw:
3.1 Information about Services
A.

text: Physical therapist assistants may provide consumers with information regarding provision of services within the pro- tocol established by a supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may provide consumers with
information regarding provision of services within the pro-
tocol established by a supervising physical therapist.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: Physical therapist assistants may not use, or participate in the use of any form of, communication containing a false, fraudulent, misleading, deceptive, unfair, or sensational statement or claim.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may not use, or participate in
the use of any form of, communication containing a false,
fraudulent, misleading, deceptive, unfair, or sensational
statement or claim.

text: 3.2 Organizational Employment Physical therapist assistants shall advise their employer(s) of any employer practice which causes them to be in conflict with the Standards of Ethical Conduct for the Physical Therapist Assistant .
text_raw:
3.2 Organizational Employment
Physical therapist assistants shall advise their employer(s) of
any employer practice which causes them to be in conflict with the
Standards of Ethical Conduct for the Physical Therapist Assistant .

text: 3.3 Endorsement of Equipment Physical therapist assistants may not endorse equipment or exer- cise influence on patients or families to purchase or lease equipment except as directed by a physical therapist acting in accord with the stipulation in paragraph 5.3.
text_raw:
3.3 Endorsement of Equipment
Physical therapist assistants may not endorse equipment or exer-
cise influence on patients or families to purchase or lease equipment
except as directed by a physical therapist acting in accord with the
stipulation in paragraph 5.3.

text: A. of the Guide for Professional Conduct.
text_raw: A. of the Guide for Professional Conduct.

text: 3.4 Financial Considerations Physical therapist assistants shall never place their own finan- cial interest above the welfare of their patients.
text_raw:
3.4 Financial Considerations
Physical therapist assistants shall never place their own finan-
cial interest above the welfare of their patients.

text: 3.5 Exploitation of Patients Physical therapist assistants shall not participate in any arrange- ments in which patients are exploited.
text_raw:
3.5 Exploitation of Patients
Physical therapist assistants shall not participate in any arrange-
ments in which patients are exploited.

text: Such arrangements include situations where referring sources enhance their personal incomes as a result of referring for, delegating, prescribing, or recommend- ing physical therapy services.
text_raw:
Such arrangements include
situations where referring sources enhance their personal incomes
as a result of referring for, delegating, prescribing, or recommend-
ing physical therapy services.

text: STANDARD 4 Physical therapist assistants provide services within the limits of the law.
text_raw:
STANDARD 4
Physical therapist assistants provide services within the limits of
the law.

text: APTA Guide for Conduct 277
text_raw: APTA Guide for Conduct 277

text: 4.1 Supervisory Relationships Physical therapist assistants shall comply with all aspects of the law.
text_raw:
4.1 Supervisory Relationships
Physical therapist assistants shall comply with all aspects of the
law.

text: Regardless of the content of any law, physical therapist assis- tants shall provide services only under the supervision and direc- tion of a physical therapist who is properly credentialed in the juris- diction in which the physical therapist assistant practices.
text_raw:
Regardless of the content of any law, physical therapist assis-
tants shall provide services only under the supervision and direc-
tion of a physical therapist who is properly credentialed in the juris-
diction in which the physical therapist assistant practices.

text: 4.2 Representation Physical therapist assistants shall not hold themselves out as physical therapists.
text_raw:
4.2 Representation
Physical therapist assistants shall not hold themselves out as
physical therapists.

text: STANDARD 5 Physical therapist assistants make those judgments that are com- mensurate with their qualifications as physical therapist assistants.
text_raw:
STANDARD 5
Physical therapist assistants make those judgments that are com-
mensurate with their qualifications as physical therapist assistants.

text: 5.1 Patient Treatment Physical therapist assistants shall report all untoward patient responses to a supervising physical therapist.
text_raw:
5.1 Patient Treatment
Physical therapist assistants shall report all untoward patient
responses to a supervising physical therapist.

text: 5.2 Patient Safety A.
text_raw:
5.2 Patient Safety
A.

text: Physical therapist assistants may refuse to carry out treat- ment procedures that they believe to be not in the best inter- est of the patient.
text_raw:
Physical therapist assistants may refuse to carry out treat-
ment procedures that they believe to be not in the best inter-
est of the patient.

text: B.
text_raw: B.

text: The physical therapist assistant shall not provide physical therapy services to a patient while under the influence of a substance that impairs his or her ability to do so safely.
text_raw:
The physical therapist assistant shall not provide physical
therapy services to a patient while under the influence of a
substance that impairs his or her ability to do so safely.

text: 5.3 Qualifications Physical therapist assistants may not carry out any procedure that they are not qualified to provide.
text_raw:
5.3 Qualifications
Physical therapist assistants may not carry out any procedure
that they are not qualified to provide.

text: 5.4 Discontinuance of Treatment Program Physical therapist assistants shall discontinue immediately any treatment procedures which in their judgment appears to be harm- ful to the patient.
text_raw:
5.4 Discontinuance of Treatment Program
Physical therapist assistants shall discontinue immediately any
treatment procedures which in their judgment appears to be harm-
ful to the patient.

text: 5.5 Continued Education Physical therapist assistants shall continue participation in vari- ous types of educational activities which enhance their skills and knowledge and provide new skills and knowledge.
text_raw:
5.5 Continued Education
Physical therapist assistants shall continue participation in vari-
ous types of educational activities which enhance their skills and
knowledge and provide new skills and knowledge.

text_raw: 278 Appendix 9

text: STANDARD 6 Physical therapist assistants accept the responsibility to protect the public and the profession from unethical, incompetent, or illegal acts.
text_raw:
STANDARD 6
Physical therapist assistants accept the responsibility to protect
the public and the profession from unethical, incompetent, or illegal
acts.

text: 6.1 Consumer Protection Physical therapist assistants shall report any conduct which appears to be unethical, incompetent, or illegal.
text_raw:
6.1 Consumer Protection
Physical therapist assistants shall report any conduct which
appears to be unethical, incompetent, or illegal.

text: PREAMBLE The physical therapy profession is committed to providing an optimum level of service delivery and to striving for excellence in practice.
text_raw:
PREAMBLE
The physical therapy profession is committed to providing an
optimum level of service delivery and to striving for excellence in
practice.

text: The House of Delegates of the American Physical Therapy Association, as the formal body that represents the profession, attests to this commitment by adopting and promoting the follow- ing Standards of Practice for Physical Therapy .
text_raw:
The House of Delegates of the American Physical Therapy
Association, as the formal body that represents the profession,
attests to this commitment by adopting and promoting the follow-
ing Standards of Practice for Physical Therapy .

text: These Standards of Practice for Physical Therapy are the profession’s statement of condi- tions and performances which are essential for the provision of high-quality physical therapy.
text_raw:
These Standards of
Practice for Physical Therapy are the profession’s statement of condi-
tions and performances which are essential for the provision of
high-quality physical therapy.

AAPPPPEENNDDIIXX 1111
American Physical Therapy Association
Guidelines for Physical Therapy Documentation
PREAMBLE
The American Physical Therapy Association (APTA) is commit-
ted to meeting the physical therapy needs of society, to meeting the
needs and interests of its members, and to developing and improv-
ing the art and science of physical therapy, including: practice, edu-
cation, and research.

text: To help meet these responsibilities, the APTA Board of Directors has approved the following guidelines for phys- ical therapy documentation.

To help meet these responsibilities, the APTA
Board of Directors has approved the following guidelines for phys-

text: It is recognized that these guidelines do not reflect all of the unique documentation requirements associ- ated with the many specialty areas within the physical therapy pro- fession.

It is recognized that these guidelines
do not reflect all of the unique documentation requirements associ-

text: Applicable for both handwritten and electronic documen- tation systems, these guidelines are intended to be used as a foun- dation for the development of more specific documentation guide- lines in specialty areas, while at the same time providing guidance for the physical therapy profession across all practice settings.

text: MISSION STATEMENT The mission of the American Physical Therapy Association (APTA), the principle membership organization representing and promoting the profession of physical therapy, is to further the pro- fession’s role in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of move- ment dysfunction and the enhancement of the physical health and functional abilities of members of the public.
text_raw:
MISSION STATEMENT
The mission of the American Physical Therapy Association
(APTA), the principle membership organization representing and
promoting the profession of physical therapy, is to further the pro-
fession’s role in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of move-
ment dysfunction and the enhancement of the physical health and
functional abilities of members of the public.

text: POLICY ON APTA MISSION STATEMENT To fulfill the American Physical Therapy Association’s (APTA) Mission to meet the needs and interests of its members and to pro- mote physical therapy as a vital professional career, the Association shall:  Promote physical therapy care and services through the establishment, maintenance, and promotion of ethical prin- ciples and quality standards for practice, education, and research;  Influence policy in the public and private sectors;  Enable physical therapy practitioners to improve their skills, knowledge, and operation in the interest of furthering the profession;  Develop and improve the art and science of physical thera- py, including practice, education, and research;  Facilitate a common understanding and appreciation for the diversity of the profession, the membership, and the com- munities we serve; and  Maintain a stable and diverse financial base from which to fund the programs, services, and operations that support this mission.
text_raw:
POLICY ON APTA MISSION STATEMENT
To fulfill the American Physical Therapy Association’s (APTA)
Mission to meet the needs and interests of its members and to pro-
mote physical therapy as a vital professional career, the Association
shall:
 Promote physical therapy care and services through the
establishment, maintenance, and promotion of ethical prin-
ciples and quality standards for practice, education, and
research;
 Influence policy in the public and private sectors;
 Enable physical therapy practitioners to improve their skills,
knowledge, and operation in the interest of furthering the
profession;
 Develop and improve the art and science of physical thera-
py, including practice, education, and research;
 Facilitate a common understanding and appreciation for the
diversity of the profession, the membership, and the com-
munities we serve; and
 Maintain a stable and diverse financial base from which to
fund the programs, services, and operations that support
this mission.

ability of the subject to perceive touch along the skin of the face.
